newsitem.title: UK: Nationalists gain ground in Scottish TV survey.
newsitem.headline: Nationalists gain ground in Scottish TV survey.

text.p: Nationalists and Liberal Democrats gained ground over the past month at the expense of Tony Blair's Labour party and Britain's ruling Conservatives in an audience survey by Scotland's two commercial television companies.

The Scottish National Party (SNP) gained three to 29 percent and Liberal Democrats two to 13 percent. Labour dropped two to 42 percent and Conservatives three to 14 percent in the survey carried out from April 3-10 by Scottish Television (STV) and Grampian Television.
Members of a 500-strong audience declared their political preferences for the first "Scottish 500" programme on March 7. They were surveyed again for the second programme on Monday.

The joint STV-Grampian series now runs each Monday and Thursday until polling day on May 1. Politicians, starting with Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown, will be questioned by the same 500 and the four Scottish party leaders will debate face- to-face in the last programme on Monday, April 28.
